item.title: Children among 139 dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says
item.description:
Larry W. Smith / Getty Images Two young children are among eight people shot dead Friday in Erie, Pennsylvania. The Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports that police initially responded to 911 calls that said a man was firing a gun outside a home. First responders reportedly arrived to find two women who were shot dead on the sidewalk outside the residence. Officers and a SWAT team surrounded the home, and a standoff ensued, according to police. Once inside, police found the other victims in what the police chief described as the “worst crime scene” he has ever witnessed. Officials said in a statement to the Post-Gazette that “the situation has been contained, the shooter is deceased, and there is no ongoing threat or danger to the public at this time.” Authorities also told the Erie Times-News that the suspected mass shooter appeared to have died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. item.title: After ICE Shooting, Progressives Want New York’s Police Commissioner to Step Down
item.description:
The ICE shooting of a 28-year-old in the Bronx Thursday has provoked an uproar among New Yorkers, who rushed to the streets in protest the night of the shooting, clashing with the New York Police Department. At least five protesters were arrested. And though members of the NYPD were not involved in the shooting, they were involved in arresting protesters and, some witnesses say, protecting ICE vehicles—despite a New York State law that prohibits local police departments from collaborating with the federal agency, as well as local “sanctuary city” laws. Allies of Mayor Zohran Mamdani are now calling on his police commissioner, Jessica Tisch, to step down if ICE does not leave New York City. Oscar Belgal, the man who was shot in his car while his five-year-old child sat in the backseat, is being hold in the MDC Brooklyn federal detention facility. He was shot at least seven times,…

item.title: What to expect as Hurricane Isaias bears down on the Gulf Coast as a major storm
item.description:
Something strange just popped up in the Gulf of Mexico: a hurricane. Well, not so much Hurricane Isaias, which strengthened into a Category 3 before its predicted landfall along the Florida Panhandle late Friday. It’s more the timing of it: This is the first Atlantic hurricane of the season, which began all the way back in June. That smashes the previous record in the satellite era for the latest first hurricane of a season, September 11. “This is pretty astounding, really, to break a record by just about a month,” said Brian McNoldy, a senior research associate who studies hurricanes at the University of Miami. So what’s with the extraordinary delay? El Niño, of all things . Even though that band of warm water is on the other side of the Americas in the Pacific, it messes with two of the fundamental ingredients for making hurricanes in the Atlantic: wind and humidity. Amid multiple reports alleging outright corruption, on-the-record quotes from Greek officials who seem to detest her grifting behavior, and my personal favorite, the criminal use of “honey” in casual conversation, it appears that Guilfoyle’s ambassadorship could be in peril. The increasingly precarious standing follows two explosive Wall Street Journal reports alleging Guilfoyle, whose personal finances seemed to be in the gutter even before her ambassadorship, repeatedly pleaded for money from Eric Deters, a Republican donor and failed congressional candidate, in return for political favors. item.title: Candidate named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru
item.description:
A politician named Hitler Mussolini Simeón Flores has won a mayoral election in Peru, securing 229 votes on a center-left party ticket. Simeón, 45, finished first in Queropalca, a district in Peru’s Huánuco region with a population of just over 730 people. Running for the Ahora Nación (Now Nation) party, he received 34.5% of the 663 valid votes cast in the election. His nearest competitor, Gaspar Benilde Osorio Zambrano of Popular Renewal Peru, received 204 votes, putting Simeón ahead by 25. His victory awaits formal proclamation by the electoral authority. Simeón’s name evokes Adolf Hitler, the leader of Nazi Germany, and Benito Mussolini, Italy’s fascist dictator and Hitler’s wartime ally. According to his candidate declaration, Simeón resigned from the populist right-wing Popular Force party in 2025 before running for Ahora Nación. item.title: Taylor Knibb wins Ironman world title after leader collapses in dramatic Kona finish
item.description:
The elite men's race at the UCI Gravel World Championships in Nannup, Western Australia, came down to a thrilling finale between four top talents, including two WorldTour pros who have made occasional appearances in gravel races. Defending champion Florian Vermeersch (Belgium) made the trip, eager to go back-to-back, and he came close after 144.5 lumpy and technical kilometres. However, it was full-time gravel rider Magnus Bak Klaris (Denmark) who outpunched the four-man group, also containing Connor Swift (Great Britain) and Mads Würtz Schmidt (Denmark). Just seven seconds after the lead group, Germany's Paul Voss led home Keegan Swenson (USA) and Martin Stosek (Czechia). Brief results: Magnus Bak Klaris (Denmark) 4:09:05 Florian Vermeersch (Belgium) st. Connor Swift (Great Britain) st. Mads Würtz Schmidt (Denmark) st. Paul Voss (Germany) +0:07 Full results here.
